settings.heading: Why so many kids just seem a little… off
settings.alt: A boy pushes peas around a full dinner plate while his mum watches
settings.text:
When your child is struggling in ways that don’t quite add up:

  • Dinners pushed around the plate
  • “My tummy hurts” right as you’re leaving for school
  • Gassy, bloated or out of sorts after meals
  • Bathroom trips all over the place
  • That general feeling your kid just isn’t their usual self

It’s easy to brush it off as a phase. And sometimes it is.

But when the same signs keep showing up and nothing you try seems to change them, it’s worth looking at the part of their body that’s busiest of all: their gut.

Between school snacks, birthday sweets, sandpits, pets and everything that ends up in little mouths, a child’s digestion has a lot on its plate every single day.
settings.warn: When digestion is out of rhythm, the whole family feels it: battles at dinner, rough school mornings, and a kid who isn’t quite themselves.
settings.good: When their tummy feels settled, kids tend to eat better, mornings get easier, and your happy, hungry kid comes back.*
settings.accordions:
🤔 Should I talk to my doctor first? | Yes, if anything worries you. See your doctor before starting if your child has ongoing or severe tummy pain, vomiting, blood in their stool, weight loss, itching around the bottom at night, or worms you can see. ParaPatrol is a daily herbal supplement for everyday tummy comfort, not a treatment for any condition.
🎒 Why are kids’ tummies so busy? | Kids explore with their hands and mouths. Shared crayons, playgrounds, sandpits, pets, school snacks and party food all keep a growing gut busy, especially in school season and after holidays.
🌿 What does a gentle herbal routine actually do? | Traditional herbs like fennel, anise and licorice have been used for generations to soothe occasional tummy upsets, while botanicals like black walnut and clove support a regular digestive rhythm.*

settings.heading: Does this sound like your child?
settings.alt: A mum zips up her son’s jacket at the front door before school
settings.intro: Every child is different. These are the signs parents tell us they notice most.
settings.items:
🍽️ | Picky eating | Pushes dinner around the plate, then wants snacks an hour later. A comfortable tummy and a healthy appetite go hand in hand.*
😣 | “My tummy hurts” | Occasional tummy aches that love to show up on school mornings.
🎈 | Gassy or bloated after meals | Little rumbles and puffy tummies after eating. Fennel and anise are classics for soothing occasional gas.*
🚽 | Irregular bathroom trips | A few days of nothing, then the opposite. Regularity is one of the clearest windows into how their tummy is doing.
🍬 | Craving snacks and sweets | Reaching for crackers and sugar instead of real meals.
🎂 | Out of sorts after parties and holidays | A run of treats can leave a tummy unsettled for days afterwards.
🏖️ | Touches everything | Sandpits, pets, playgrounds and shared toys keep little tummies busy.
🌅 | Rough mornings | Grumpy, hungry-but-won’t-eat starts that set the tone for the whole day.
settings.banner: Nodding along to 2 or more? Their tummy could use a little gentle, daily support.* If you’ve seen worms, night-time itching, blood in their stool or ongoing pain, please see your doctor first.

settings.heading: Fits into your morning in 30 seconds
settings.alt: A dropper of ParaPatrol going into a glass of juice
settings.text:
ParaPatrol is a gentle, once-a-day dropper, not a harsh cleanse. No special diets, no days off school, no bathroom emergencies.

It mixes straight into juice, milk or a smoothie, so it slips into the school-run routine without a fight.
settings.steps:
Shake well and fill the dropper to the 1 mL line.
Mix into juice, milk or a smoothie. Orange juice and berry smoothies hide the herbal taste best.
Give once a day with food for 2–3 weeks, then take a break.
settings.accordions:
✅ Zero prep | No mixing powders, no pills to hide, no diet changes. Just one dropper in a drink.
😋 Will my picky eater take it? | It has a natural raspberry flavour and a bitter blocker. Most kids drink it in juice without a fuss. Starting with half a dropper for the first few days helps too.
📅 How often should we use it? | Use it daily for a 2–3 week routine, then take a break. Many parents keep a bottle on hand for school terms and after holidays or trips.
🛒 How many bottles do I need? | One 30 mL bottle holds about 30 servings, enough for one child’s full 2–3 week routine. For two kids, or to have a routine ready for the next school term, choose a bundle.

settings.heading: Your questions answered
settings.items:
What age can my child start? | ParaPatrol is made and dosed for kids 3 and up. It is not for children under 3.
How fast will I see a difference? | Every child is different. Many parents notice settled tummies and better appetites within 1–2 weeks of daily use.*
What does it taste like? | A natural raspberry flavour with a bitter blocker to soften the herbal taste. Mixed into orange juice or a berry smoothie, most kids drink it without a fuss.
Is it safe? What about side effects? | Stop use and talk to your doctor if your child has vomiting, diarrhea, stomach pain or any unusual reaction. Start with half a dropper for the first few days if your child has a sensitive tummy.
Can we use it with other supplements or medication? | If your child takes medication or has a health condition, talk to your pediatrician first. Bring the bottle so they can see the full ingredient list.
What if my child has a nut allergy? | ParaPatrol contains tree nut (black walnut), so it is not for kids with a tree nut allergy.
Does it contain alcohol or sugar? | No alcohol and no sugar. It is also gluten-free.
What if we miss a day? | Just carry on the next day with the usual dose. Don’t double up.
How does the guarantee work? | Try ParaPatrol for 30 days. If you’re not happy, contact our team and we’ll refund you.
How long does shipping take? | Orders are usually processed within 1–2 business days and most arrive within 7–15 days. Shipping is free on every order.
